claims.text: Equiatomic CrCoNi has a superior combination of strength and ductility relative to equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
CrCoNi has a lower stacking-fault energy than CrMnFeCoNi.
The absence of Mn in CrCoNi permits magnetic ordering that lowers the energy barrier for forming HCP regions.
Deformation produces nanoscale HCP regions in CrCoNi that are localized at stacking faults and twin or other internal boundaries.
The deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation in CrCoNi is triggered by dislocation slip and interactions with internal boundaries.
Low stacking-fault energy permits dislocation dissociation and overlapping stacking faults that initiate the FCC-to-HCP transformation.
The nanoscale HCP regions impede dislocations and interact with twin boundaries, thereby increasing work hardening.
The HCP transformation can increase strength without compromising plastic deformation in CrCoNi.
Mn in CrMnFeCoNi introduces magnetic frustration that removes the FCC-HCP energetic driving force and suppresses the transformation.
Identically processed equiatomic CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi can both begin as single-phase FCC solid solutions.
CrMnFeCoNi does not develop the additional deformation-induced nanoscale HCP phase observed in CrCoNi.
Cryogenic deformation makes deformation-induced twinning and phase transformation more pronounced in these alloys.
Relative to CrMnFeCoNi, deformed CrCoNi should contain a higher density of nanoscale HCP regions at deformation defects.
Relative to CrMnFeCoNi, CrCoNi should have a higher strain-hardening rate under identical cryogenic deformation conditions.
Relative to CrMnFeCoNi, CrCoNi should show an improved balance of strength and ductility under identical deformation conditions.

The proposed mechanism applies when processing yields a uniform initial FCC phase and deformation produces stacking faults and twins, particularly at cryogenic temperature and moderate-to-high strain.
The quantitative HCP phase-fraction difference and the HCP phase's precise contribution to macroscopic properties remain undetermined.
The proposed mechanism is sensitive to minor changes in processing or testing parameters.

The hypothesis would be falsified if identically tested CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi show no significant difference in HCP formation, or if CrCoNi does not exceed CrMnFeCoNi in strain hardening and overall mechanical performance.
